metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: No HTTPS encryption (plain HTTP only) finding template with comprehensive migration guidance for all audiences including SSL/TLS certificate acquisition, infrastructure deployment procedures, and organizational change management for transitioning from HTTP to HTTPS.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your website operates entirely over unencrypted HTTP, transmitting all data in plain text visible to anyone on the network path. This is a CRITICAL security vulnerability requiring immediate remediation.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: ALL user data transmitted in cleartext: passwords, credit cards, personal information, session tokens. Network attackers can read, modify, or steal any data. Guaranteed PCI-DSS compliance failure - cannot process payments without HTTPS. Modern browsers display prominent 'Not Secure' warnings, damaging trust and conversion rates. Google penalizes HTTP sites in search rankings. Potential for massive data breach with regulatory fines (GDPR: up to €20M or 4% revenue, PCI-DSS: $5,000-$100,000/month).
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: IMMEDIATE COMPLIANCE FAILURE: PCI-DSS mandates HTTPS for all payment processing - cannot accept credit cards without it. GDPR Article 32 requires encryption of personal data in transit - violation risks mandatory breach notification and fines. HIPAA requires encryption for PHI transmission. SOC 2 Type II requires transport encryption. This is a show-stopper for all security certifications and audits.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Site operates on unencrypted HTTP instead of secure HTTPS, creating CRITICAL security vulnerability and blocking all compliance certifications. Migration to HTTPS required immediately.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: CRITICAL PRIORITY - must be addressed before any other work. Typical HTTPS migration: 1-2 days for small sites, 1-2 weeks for complex applications. Requires coordination across infrastructure, development, QA teams. Blocks: payment processing, user authentication, PCI-DSS compliance, security audits, production launches.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 4-8 hours for simple site: 2 hours SSL certificate acquisition, 2 hours server configuration, 2 hours testing, 2 hours deployment. Complex sites with mixed content, third-party integrations, hardcoded URLs: 2-4 weeks. Factor in QA testing, code changes, configuration updates across all environments.
dependencies: SSL/TLS certificate purchase or Let's Encrypt setup
Server configuration access (Nginx, Apache, IIS, CDN)
Code review for hardcoded http:// URLs
Budget approval for SSL certificate (if not using free option)
Coordinate with payment processor for HTTPS requirement

DEVELOPER.summary: Site serves content over unencrypted HTTP protocol instead of HTTPS (HTTP over TLS/SSL), exposing all data to network interception.
DEVELOPER.technical: HTTP transmits data in plain text without encryption. All form submissions, cookies, API calls, user credentials, and session tokens are visible to anyone monitoring network traffic. HTTPS wraps HTTP in TLS/SSL encryption, making data unreadable to eavesdroppers. Migration requires: (1) Obtain SSL/TLS certificate, (2) Configure web server to handle HTTPS on port 443, (3) Update application code to use https:// URLs, (4) Implement HTTP→HTTPS redirects, (5) Add HSTS headers, (6) Fix mixed content warnings (HTTP resources on HTTPS pages).
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: Cleartext transmission of sensitive information (CWE-319). Network sniffing attacks can capture passwords, session cookies, API keys, personal data, payment information. Man-in-the-middle attacks can modify responses, inject malicious code, steal credentials. No authentication of server identity - users cannot verify they're communicating with legitimate server. Violates basic security principle: encryption in transit.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: CRITICAL VULNERABILITY: Complete absence of transport encryption allows trivial interception and modification of all traffic.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: Cleartext protocol vulnerability (CWE-319, CWE-311). Zero encryption protection. All HTTP traffic visible to: ISPs, network administrators, WiFi operators, VPN providers, government surveillance, corporate proxies, malicious actors on network path. Password sniffing, session hijacking, and man-in-the-middle attacks require minimal technical sophistication - automated tools readily available.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Passive sniffing: Attacker monitors network traffic (WiFi, router, ISP level) using Wireshark, tcpdump, or similar tools. All data captured in plaintext. Active MITM: Attacker positions between client and server, intercepts and potentially modifies traffic in real-time. Can inject malicious JavaScript, steal credentials, redirect to phishing sites. Public WiFi networks are high-risk hunting grounds. 100% of traffic is compromised, not just specific requests.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: CRITICAL - This is a fundamental security failure. Every connection is vulnerable. Users on public networks (airports, coffee shops, hotels) face guaranteed compromise. Attackers with network access can capture passwords on first login attempt. Session tokens can be stolen and used for account takeover. Payment data transmitted in clear text. This vulnerability makes all other security controls irrelevant - if attacker can read everything, authentication, authorization, and data protection measures provide no benefit.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: IMMEDIATE - STOP ALL DATA COLLECTION. Do not allow users to submit passwords, personal information, or payment data until HTTPS is deployed. This is a zero-day, always-exploited vulnerability. Every minute of operation over HTTP increases breach likelihood. Prioritize over ALL other work. Recommend taking site offline for sensitive operations until HTTPS implemented.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Web servers configured to listen only on HTTP port 80 without TLS/SSL encryption on port 443. CRITICAL infrastructure security gap requiring immediate SSL/TLS deployment.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: Server accepts connections on TCP port 80 (HTTP) but not port 443 (HTTPS). No SSL/TLS certificate installed or configured. Web server (Nginx, Apache, IIS) not configured for HTTPS virtual hosts. Load balancers and reverse proxies not performing SSL termination. CDN (if used) not configured for HTTPS delivery. DNS records may not point to HTTPS-capable infrastructure.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: ALL web servers, load balancers, CDN configurations, reverse proxies in entire infrastructure stack. Affects: production, staging, development environments. Impacts: primary domain and all subdomains. Related services: APIs, admin panels, user dashboards, payment systems, authentication endpoints. Any endpoint accepting user data is CRITICAL risk.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Current state: All traffic over port 80 (HTTP). Target state: All traffic over port 443 (HTTPS) with HTTP→HTTPS redirects. Monitor: Certificate expiration dates (Let's Encrypt: 90 days, commercial: 1-2 years), TLS version and cipher strength, mixed content warnings, SSL Labs grade (target: A or A+), browser security warnings, HTTPS adoption metrics, redirect chain performance.

QA_TESTER.summary: Cannot perform security testing or validate data protection without HTTPS. All test accounts, test data, and testing credentials transmitted in cleartext, compromising test environment security.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Security scanning tools will fail with CRITICAL severity. Cannot test: secure authentication flows, payment processing, session management, cookie security (Secure flag requires HTTPS), Content Security Policy, HSTS enforcement, CORS with credentials. Browser automation (Selenium, Playwright) shows security warnings. Cannot verify encryption of sensitive data in transit. API testing exposes test credentials to network monitoring.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Complete security testing blockage. Cannot certify application security. PCI-DSS compliance testing impossible. Penetration testing will immediately identify this as critical finding. User acceptance testing on production will expose real user credentials. Cannot obtain security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001). Automated security scanners will fail entire test suite. Browser compatibility testing complicated by security warnings.

letsencrypt-certbot.config:
# Let's Encrypt (Free SSL Certificate) - Recommended for most sites
# Supports automatic renewal every 90 days

# Install Certbot (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt update
sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx  # For Nginx
# OR
sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-apache  # For Apache

# Obtain certificate (Nginx - automatic configuration)
sudo certbot --nginx -d yourdomain.com -d www.yourdomain.com

# Obtain certificate (Apache - automatic configuration)
sudo certbot --apache -d yourdomain.com -d www.yourdomain.com

# Manual certificate only (you configure web server yourself)
sudo certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/html -d yourdomain.com

# Test automatic renewal
sudo certbot renew --dry-run

# Certificate locations after installation:
# Certificate: /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/fullchain.pem
# Private Key: /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/privkey.pem
letsencrypt-certbot.reload:
# Certbot automatically configures and reloads web server
# If manual changes needed:
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
# OR
sudo apache2ctl configtest && sudo systemctl reload apache2

# Set up automatic renewal (usually configured automatically)
sudo systemctl status certbot.timer

# Manual renewal test
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
letsencrypt-certbot.verify:
# Verify HTTPS is working
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# Check certificate details
echo | openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -servername yourdomain.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

# Test SSL configuration
ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=yourdomain.com

nginx.enable:
# Enable new configuration
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/yourdomain.com /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/

# Test configuration
sudo nginx -t

# Reload Nginx
sudo systemctl reload nginx

# Verify Nginx is running
sudo systemctl status nginx
nginx.verify:
# Test HTTPS
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# Test HTTP redirect
curl -I http://yourdomain.com

# Should see 301 redirect to HTTPS

# Check certificate
echo | openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -servername yourdomain.com

apache.config:
# Apache HTTPS Configuration
# File: /etc/apache2/sites-available/yourdomain-ssl.conf

<IfModule mod_ssl.c>
    <VirtualHost *:443>
        ServerName yourdomain.com
        ServerAlias www.yourdomain.com
        DocumentRoot /var/www/html

        # SSL Engine
        SSLEngine on
        
        # SSL Certificate Files
        SSLCertificateFile /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/fullchain.pem
        SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/letsencrypt/live/yourdomain.com/privkey.pem

        # Modern SSL Configuration
        SSLProtocol all -SSLv3 -TLSv1 -TLSv1.1
        SSLCipherSuite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
        SSLHonorCipherOrder on

        # HSTS Header (after testing)
        Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"

        <Directory /var/www/html>
            Options Indexes FollowSymLinks
            AllowOverride All
            Require all granted
        </Directory>

        ErrorLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/error.log
        CustomLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/access.log combined
    </VirtualHost>
</IfModule>

# HTTP to HTTPS Redirect
# File: /etc/apache2/sites-available/yourdomain.conf
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    ServerAlias www.yourdomain.com
    
    # Redirect all HTTP to HTTPS
    Redirect permanent / https://yourdomain.com/
</VirtualHost>
apache.enable:
# Enable required modules
sudo a2enmod ssl
sudo a2enmod headers
sudo a2enmod rewrite

# Enable SSL site
sudo a2ensite yourdomain-ssl.conf

# Test configuration
sudo apache2ctl configtest

# Reload Apache
sudo systemctl reload apache2

# Verify
sudo systemctl status apache2
apache.verify:
# Test HTTPS
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# Test redirect
curl -I http://yourdomain.com

# Check logs if issues
sudo tail -f /var/log/apache2/error.log

cloudflare.config:
# Cloudflare SSL Configuration (Easiest Option)
# Free SSL certificate included with Cloudflare

# Step 1: Add site to Cloudflare
# 1. Create account at cloudflare.com
# 2. Add your domain
# 3. Update nameservers at domain registrar to Cloudflare's nameservers
# 4. Wait for DNS propagation (5-60 minutes)

# Step 2: Enable SSL/TLS
# 1. Go to SSL/TLS tab in Cloudflare dashboard
# 2. Set SSL/TLS encryption mode:
#    - Flexible: Cloudflare↔User HTTPS, Cloudflare↔Origin HTTP (quick start)
#    - Full: Cloudflare↔User HTTPS, Cloudflare↔Origin HTTPS (self-signed OK)
#    - Full (Strict): All HTTPS with valid certificates (recommended)

# Step 3: Enable "Always Use HTTPS"
# 1. Go to SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates
# 2. Toggle "Always Use HTTPS" to On
# 3. This automatically redirects all HTTP to HTTPS

# Step 4: Enable HSTS (after testing)
# 1. SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates → HSTS
# 2. Enable with recommended settings

# Origin Server Configuration (for Full Strict mode):
# Install Cloudflare Origin Certificate on your server
# 1. SSL/TLS → Origin Server → Create Certificate
# 2. Install on your web server (Nginx/Apache)
# 3. Configure server to accept HTTPS on port 443
cloudflare.verify:
# Test HTTPS
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# Verify Cloudflare is active
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i cf-ray

# Check SSL Labs
https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=yourdomain.com

aws-acm.config:
# AWS Certificate Manager + Application Load Balancer
# Free SSL certificates for AWS resources

# Step 1: Request Certificate in ACM
aws acm request-certificate \
  --domain-name yourdomain.com \
  --subject-alternative-names www.yourdomain.com \
  --validation-method DNS \
  --region us-east-1

# Step 2: Validate Domain Ownership
# Follow DNS validation instructions in ACM console
# Add CNAME records provided by ACM to your DNS

# Step 3: Attach Certificate to Load Balancer
# Via AWS Console:
# EC2 → Load Balancers → Select your ALB → Listeners → Add listener
# Protocol: HTTPS, Port: 443, Default action: Forward to target group
# Security policy: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01
# Select ACM certificate

# Step 4: Add HTTP→HTTPS Redirect
# Edit HTTP:80 listener → Edit rules → Add redirect to HTTPS:443

# Via AWS CLI:
aws elbv2 create-listener \
  --load-balancer-arn <your-alb-arn> \
  --protocol HTTPS \
  --port 443 \
  --certificates CertificateArn=<your-cert-arn> \
  --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=<your-target-group-arn>
aws-acm.verify:
# Test ALB HTTPS endpoint
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# Verify certificate in ACM console
aws acm describe-certificate --certificate-arn <your-cert-arn>

# Check ALB listeners
aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn <your-alb-arn>

verificationSteps: 6. Verify certificate validity: openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443
8. Test across all subdomains and paths
9. Verify in multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
10. Check for mixed content warnings (HTTP resources on HTTPS page)
11. Update all hardcoded http:// URLs to https:// or protocol-relative
12. Test payment processing and third-party integrations
13. Enable HSTS header after confirming HTTPS stability
14. Set up certificate renewal automation (Let's Encrypt: 90-day expiry)
15. Document certificate renewal process and calendar reminders
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
HTTPS migration should NOT be rolled back. If issues occur:
1. Keep HTTPS enabled, fix issues forward
2. If certificate invalid: obtain new certificate immediately
3. If mixed content: identify and fix HTTP resources
4. If third-party integration breaks: update integration to HTTPS
5. Temporary: remove HSTS header if testing needed (allow HTTP temporarily)
6. Never redirect HTTPS back to HTTP - security regression
7. Communication plan: inform users of temporary issues, ETA for fix
8. Rollback only if complete site outage with no forward fix available

manualTests.name: HTTPS Access Test
steps: 1. Open browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
2. Navigate to https://yourdomain.com
3. Check address bar for padlock icon
4. Click padlock → View certificate details
5. Verify certificate is valid (not expired, correct domain)
6. Verify connection shows 'Secure' or equivalent
7. Test main navigation, all pages load over HTTPS
8. Check for mixed content warnings in DevTools Console
manualTests.expected: Site loads successfully over HTTPS with valid certificate, no security warnings, padlock icon displayed in all browsers

manualTests.name: HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Test
steps: 1. Type http://yourdomain.com in address bar (explicitly HTTP)
2. Press Enter
3. Observe browser behavior
4. Check final URL in address bar
5. Open DevTools Network tab, repeat test
6. Verify 301 or 302 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS
7. Test with www and non-www variants
8. Test deep links: http://yourdomain.com/page/subpage
manualTests.expected: All HTTP requests automatically redirect to HTTPS via 301/302, preserving path and query parameters

manualTests.name: Mixed Content Detection Test
steps: 1. Load site over HTTPS
2. Open DevTools Console (F12)
3. Look for mixed content warnings (yellow/red shield icon)
4. Identify any HTTP resources loaded on HTTPS page
5. Check: images, CSS, JavaScript, iframes, video
6. Test forms submission over HTTPS
7. Verify all AJAX/API calls use HTTPS
manualTests.expected: No mixed content warnings. All resources (images, scripts, styles) loaded over HTTPS

manualTests.name: Certificate Validation Test
steps: 1. Visit https://yourdomain.com
2. Click padlock icon → Certificate details
3. Verify: Issued To matches your domain
4. Verify: Issuer is trusted CA (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.)
5. Verify: Valid From date is in past
6. Verify: Valid To date is in future (not expired)
7. Verify: Subject Alternative Names includes all domain variants
8. Test subdomains if wildcard certificate
manualTests.expected: Certificate valid, trusted, covers all required domains, not expired or expiring soon

edgeCases: Test with certificate expired or not yet valid
Test with self-signed certificate (should show warning)
Test subdomain access with wildcard vs specific certificate
Test on mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Android Chrome)
Test with strict certificate validation in automation tools
Verify WebSocket connections upgrade to wss://
Test Service Worker with HTTPS requirement
Test payment integrations (Stripe, PayPal require HTTPS)
Verify social media sharing preview generation over HTTPS
